////WEB REPORT//// THIS OPERATION RAISES HOGS AND MAY GENERATE ROUTINE AIR EMISSIONS OF AMMONIA AND HYDROGEN SULFIDE IN EXCESS OF THE REPORTABLE QUANTITY OF 100 POUNDS PER 24 HOURS. A ROUGH ESTIMATE OF THOSE EMISSIONS FOR THIS FARM IS 100.1 POUNDS OF AMMONIA AND 23.7 POUNDS OF HYDROGEN SULFIDE PER 24 HOURS, BUT THIS ESTIMATE COULD BE SUBSTANTIALLY ABOVE OR BELOW THE ACTUAL EMISSION RATE. Report Description
///THIS IS AN UPDATE TO REPORT #1122770. /// CALLER STATED THAT ONE TRAIN RAN INTO ANOTHER TRAIN CAUSING THE LOCOMOTIVE OF THE REAR TRAIN TO DERAIL ONTO ITS SIDE RESULTING IN A DISCHARGE OF AT LEAST 200 GALLONS OF DIESEL FUEL. NO WATERWAYS WERE IMPACTED. BOTH THE ENGINEER AND CONDUCTOR WERE INJURED AND SENT TO THE HOSPITAL WITH NON LIFE THREATENING INJURIES. CALLER ALSO STATED THAT THIS WILL MOST LIKELY REACH THE 150,000 DOLLAR DAMAGE THRESHOLD. THE REAR CAR OF THE FIRST TRAIN WAS AN EMPTY TANK AND LAST CONTAINED SODIUM HYDROXIDE, BUT NO REPORTS OF LEAKS AT THIS TIME. UPDATED INFORMATION; A TANK CAR THAT DERAILED (SHPX 204807) WAS DISCOVERED TO HAVE SPILLED 23,000 GALLONS OF LUBRICATING OIL (BASE LUBE OIL). AN UNKNOWN AMOUNT OF THE OIL ENTERED A CREEK. BOOMS HAVE BEEN PLACED IN THE CREEK TO TRY TO CONTAIN THE SPILL. A BYSTANDER IN THE AREA OF THE INCIDENT WAS INJURED. THE PERSON WAS TAKEN TO A HOSPITAL WITH UNKNOWN INJURIES.

Report DescriptionDESCRIPTION OF SPILL SITE AND SURROUNDING AREA: THERE WAS AN OVERFLOW OF WASTER THROUGH THE BYPASS ON THE 6TH, 7TH AND 8TH OF NOV. THERE WAS EXCESS RAIN ON THE 6TH. ON THE 7TH AND 8TH GATES WERE LOWERED WHICH RELEASED EXCESS SEWAGE THROUGH THE USUAL WATERWAYS. DESCRIPTION OF SPILL SOURCE, CIRCUMSTANCES, CAUSE AND ADVERSE EFFECTS OF THE SPILL: AN OVERFLOW WAS CAUSED WHILE THE MAIN PROCESSOR FOR THE PLANT WAS BEING REPLACED OVER THREE DAYS. A SMALL AMOUNT OF SEWAGE WAS NOT CONTROLLED DURING MAINTENANCE. THE PROCESSOR WAS REPLACED WITH A HIGHER CAPACITY PROCESSOR. DURING THE REPLACEMENT THERE WAS AN OVER RELEASE. THE PLAN WAS TO LOWER GATES AS A SAFETY MEASURE AS IT WAS THOUGHT LESS RISKY THAN SHUTTING THE PLANT DOWN FOR MAINTENANCE.
